components.notes: Durrett p. 56: convergence in probability (P(|Y_n-Y|>eps)->0) and the uncorrelated family (E X_i^2 < inf, E(X_iX_j)=EX_iEX_j, i != j); p. 59: arrays X_{n,k}, 1<=k<=n, row independence, no assumption between rows. All present at body 24-41, with mean-square convergence defined for the L2 conclusions. i.i.d. is defined earlier on the route (independent-random-variables.tex 68-70).

Theorem 2.2.1 with its square expansion and cross-term cancellation (annex 12-29), var(cY)=c^2 var(Y) (annex 30-31), Lemma 2.2.2 by Markov/Chebyshev with the explicit bound (body 47-50, annex 33-36), Theorem 2.2.3 in L2 and in probability (body 51-58, annex 37-44), Theorem 2.2.6 for an arbitrary sequence S_n with no sum or independence assumption (body 59-65, annex 45-52). The p. 58 i.i.d. remark is carried in substance: item 3 applies verbatim to i.i.d. finite-variance sequences and the announced weakening to E|X_i| < inf is thm:p15-direct-integrable-weak-law (body 278-286); the editorial phrase 'most important special case' is not reproduced.

Example 2.2.4 (pp. 58): definition of f_n, sup |f_n - f| -> 0, Bernoulli representation E f(S_n/n) = f_n(p), variance p(1-p)/n <= 1/(4n), uniform continuity, the split at delta and the 2M tail term are all written (annex 58-94), with an explicit uniform bound. The source's methodological remark (the weak law motivates f_n, but uniformity needs the proof's variance bound, not the result) is carried in substance by annex 77-79 and 90-93 ('The bound is independent of x ... uniform convergence, rather than just convergence at each fixed x').

Example 2.2.5 (p. 59): Y_i = X_i^2 independent, EY_i = 1/3, variance bound, Chebyshev, the set A_{n,eps} and |A_{n,eps} cap (-1,1)^n|/2^n -> 1 for every eps > 0; the reading that most of the cube's volume lies in this thin shell about radius sqrt(n/3) is stated with an explicit bound (body 105-108).

Example 2.2.7 set-up (pp. 59-60: tau_k^n, tau_0^n = 0, T_n = tau_n^n, waiting times) and Example 2.2.8 set-up (p. 60: uniform permutation, cycle listing from the smallest unused label, closing-parenthesis indicators, number of cycles) are defined, with measurability and the geometric law convention.

components.gap: owned by w02c-p15-015: the source's concrete case of Example 2.2.7 (Durrett author Version 5, p. 60) is not supplied in full. Durrett takes n = 365 as 'the number of people we need to meet until we have seen someone with every birthday', says that 'the limit theorem says it will take about 365 log 365 = 2153.46 tries to get a complete set', and notes that 'the number of trials is 5.89 times the number of birthdays'. Body lines 151-154 and annex lines 203-207 give only the two model quantities 365 log 365 ~ 2153.46 and 365 H_365 ~ 2364.65 'in the specified uniform-coupon model': the birthday reading, the source's reading of 2153.46 as the number of tries the limit theorem predicts, and the 5.89 ratio claim are absent. Supply the source's full n = 365 example with these three claims (any qualification, such as the exact expectation, may be kept alongside them).

components.notes: Independence and geometric laws with parameter 1-(k-1)/n, E T_n, the variance bound, the harmonic bounds (2.2.1), b_n = n log n and both weak limits are stated and proved (annex 133-202), including the geometric moments of Example 1.6.14 (p. 35, opened). The concrete n = 365 example is narrowed: see gap.

Lemma 2.2.9 (p. 61) with the sequential generation, its uniformity and the closing probability 1/(n-k+1) at every history; ES_n = H_n, var <= ES_n; b_n = (log n)^{1/2+eps}; S_n/log n -> 1; the worked permutation (3,9,6,8,2,1,5,4,7) -> (136)(2975)(48) and X_{9,3} = X_{9,7} = X_{9,9} = 1; the source's claim that (*) fails at eps = 0 is proved by the bounded fourth-moment lemma (exists on the route, earlier) and its CLT treatment (Example 3.4.11, verified in the source) is pointed to.

Example 2.2.10 (pp. 61-62): P(A_i), E N_n, the full second-moment expansion with diagonal and off-diagonal terms, the logarithm calculation the source defers to Lemma 3.1.1 (proved here), var(N_n)/n^2 -> 0 and N_n/n -> e^{-c} at b_n = n.

Section 2.2.3 (p. 62): deletion truncation X 1(|X| <= M) applied to row entries at b_n, the row sums, the truncated sum and the center a_n = sum E X-bar_{n,k}; the source's aim (weak laws without second moments by truncation plus Chebyshev) is stated at body 5-8.

Theorem 2.2.11 (pp. 62-63): row independence, b_n > 0, b_n -> inf, conditions (i) and (ii), (S_n - a_n)/b_n -> 0; the union-bound and Chebyshev proof is written in full; the role of the general theorem (its conditions are verified later in the i.i.d. case) is visible at annex 393-424.

Handbook-supplied lemma for the necessity direction; first-crossing decomposition, independence of the future sum, its symmetry, the strict and non-strict versions and the increment corollary are all written.

Theorem 2.2.12 (p. 63) with mu_n = E(X_1 1(|X_1| <= n)); its proof via Theorem 2.2.11 with b_n = n, Lemma 2.2.13 (stated and proved by Tonelli at strong-law-rates-and-normalization 41-67 and annex 10-60, citing pp. 63-64), the truncated second-moment identity with the endpoint at n, boundedness of g and bounded convergence (annex 393-424). The p. 63 remark (necessity) is proved independently (annex 426-478) and the Feller route is supplied elsewhere (C015). The p. 64 remark (E|X_1|^{1-eps} < inf, so the assumption is not much weaker than a finite mean) is body 270-272 with proof annex 493-501; 'need not imply a finite first absolute moment' is witnessed by item 5 of the counterexample theorem. All deterministic centers are characterized (annex 480-491).
Theorem 2.2.14 (p. 64): two dominated-convergence calculations, Theorem 2.2.12, and the eps/2 split, all written.

Handbook boundary set (not a Durrett pp. 56-64 item): every one of the six cases is computed in the annex; the almost-sure limsup in item 5 rests on the earlier proved Feller tail-series dichotomy with a_n = n, and existence of the i.i.d. sequences on the countable product construction.

Both locators opened: Durrett p. 63 remark cites Feller Vol. II (1971) pp. 234-236; Feller 2nd ed. VII.7 (pp. 234-237) proves Theorem 1 with V.(5.6), V.(5.10), V.(5.7) in that order and a median. The handbook supplies that median chain and each cited inequality with written proofs (V.5 opened at pp. 148-149 for the statements); VII.7 Theorem 2 is supplied in the infinite-mean chapter. Every other pointer resolves to an on-route treatment of the named item (Examples 2.2.15-16 at pp. 65-66; Example 3.4.11 verified to be cycles and records). Completeness of those other units' own extents is assessed in those units.
